### The Reconciliation
144 lines · 5 blocks · 1 residual · 0 .fam-* deps

```html
<!-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     RECIPE 4 · THE RECONCILIATION
     the invariant → the sources → the residual → the disposition.
     The invariant comes FIRST and it is the whole recipe: without a stated rule that says
     these numbers must agree, a discrepancy is just two facts sitting next to each other.
     Needs: proof-theme.css + proof-blocks.css.  No .fam-* ancestor.  Zero JS.
     ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

<!-- MOVE 1 · STATE THE INVARIANT.
     One sentence, of the form "X must equal Y because …". If you cannot write it, stop:
     you do not have a reconciliation. See the failure branch. -->
<section class="mod open" id="rc-invariant">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">The invariant</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">thesis</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#rc-invariant" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="thesis-block">
      <div class="ib-lab">The rule that says these numbers cannot both be right</div>
      <!-- SLOT · the invariant, as a rule about the world — not a hope about the data. -->
      <p class="ib-t">A contrast ratio between two fixed tokens is a <em>pure function of two hex values</em>. It has exactly one value. Two readings of the same pair cannot both be correct.</p>
      <!-- SLOT · name every source, and confirm they are INDEPENDENT. Re-running one source
           is a re-run, not a second measurement, and cannot reconcile anything. -->
      <p class="ib-d">Two strands measured <code>--defect</code> on <code>--defect-bg</code> on the same night, in the same token file, by different routes: one as part of a negation study, one as part of a 20-reading conformance sweep. <b>Independent instruments, identical target.</b></p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">as-of</b><span class="fv">2026-07-31</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">headfoot_PROVE.md L33, L80, L110</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 2 · THE MANIFEST — every source as a row, with its value, its method and its as-of.
     The as-of column is not decoration: a discrepancy between two different windows is TIME,
     not error, and the column is what lets a reader tell those apart without asking you.
     The last row is the CHECKSUM. It is computed, never typed. -->
<section class="mod" id="rc-manifest">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">The sources</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">table --total</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#rc-manifest" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="tablewrap">
      <table class="data">
        <thead>
          <tr><th>Source</th><th>Method</th><th class="num">Reading</th><th class="num">As of</th><th>Verdict</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <!-- SLOT · one row per independent source. -->
          <tr><td><span class="cellname">Negation study</span></td><td>single pair, read directly</td><td class="num">4.39&nbsp;:&nbsp;1</td><td class="num">07&#8209;31</td><td><span class="pill bad">breach</span></td></tr>
          <tr><td><span class="cellname">Conformance sweep</span></td><td>20 readings, worst-case reported</td><td class="num">4.74&nbsp;:&nbsp;1</td><td class="num">07&#8209;31</td><td><span class="pill ok">clears</span></td></tr>
          <tr class="total"><td><span class="cellname">Residual</span></td><td>must be 0.00 under the invariant</td><td class="num d-down">0.35</td><td class="num">&mdash;</td><td><span class="pill bad">unreconciled</span></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">windows</b><span class="fv">identical &mdash; time is not the explanation</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">[HF:negation] &middot; [HF:fan]</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 3 · BOTH SOURCES, VERBATIM, ADJACENT.
     Quote them; do not summarise them. The single most common failure of a reconciliation
     page is a paraphrase that has already resolved the conflict on the reader's behalf. -->
<section class="mod" id="rc-sources">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">In their own words</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">quote</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#rc-sources" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">

    <div class="cite">

    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">edits</b><span class="fv">none &mdash; quoted, not paraphrased</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">headfoot_PROVE.md Claim 9</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 4 · THE DISPOSITION.
     Four dispositions, and exactly one of them is chosen: measurement error · definition
     drift · time drift · real defect. UNRESOLVED is a legitimate fifth, and it is the one
     most pages refuse to write. Writing it is cheaper than being wrong. -->
<section class="mod" id="rc-disposition">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">Disposition</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">callout</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#rc-disposition" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="callout caution">
      <span class="ci" aria-hidden="true">&#9888;</span>
      <div>
        <div class="ctitle">Unresolved &mdash; and deliberately left open</div>
        <!-- SLOT · say what you ruled out, what remains, and what would settle it. -->
        <div class="cbody">Time drift is ruled out (same night, same file). Definition drift is the live hypothesis &mdash; one reading may be the token pair as authored, the other the pair as composited over the paper grain. <b>Neither strand recorded which.</b> What would settle it: one re-measurement that states its compositing context. Until then the page presents the pair as contested and <b>does not pick a winner</b>.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="callout note">
      <span class="ci" aria-hidden="true">&#9432;</span>
      <div>
        <div class="ctitle">The reconciliation that did balance</div>
        <!-- SLOT · if another reconciliation on the same page balanced, show it. A page that
             only ever shows failures teaches the reader that the checksum never passes. -->
        <div class="cbody">The corpus count reconciles exactly: <b>164 files found = 103 composed + 61 with no kit markup</b>, residual <b>0</b>. Same page, same method, a clean checksum &mdash; which is what makes the 0.35 above readable as a real signal rather than as this page's house style.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv checked">checked-here</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">disposition</b><span class="fv">unresolved &middot; 1 of 2 hypotheses eliminated</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">zone/histogram.json &middot; corpus block</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 5 · THE KEY. -->
<section class="mod flat" id="rc-legend">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">How to read the manifest</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">legend</span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="legendbox">
      <div class="row"><span class="mk pill ok">clears</span><span class="rowtext"><b>This source says the check passes.</b> The word is the channel.</span></div>
      <div class="row"><span class="mk pill bad">breach</span><span class="rowtext"><b>This source says the check fails.</b> Two rows carrying different pills on the same target is the finding, not an error in the table.</span></div>
      <div class="row"><span class="mk pill bad">unreconciled</span><span class="rowtext"><b>The residual is non-zero.</b> A residual row is present even when it is zero &mdash; a checksum you only print when it fails is not a checksum.</span></div>
      <div class="row"><span class="mk chip up">trusted-upstream</span><span class="rowtext">Both readings are carried, not re-derived. <b>This page did not re-measure either one</b>, and says so rather than implying an adjudication it did not perform.</span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

### The Decision Brief
159 lines · 4 blocks · 3 options · 0 .fam-* deps

```html
<!-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     RECIPE 5 · THE DECISION BRIEF
     the question → the options with their real costs → the lean → the falsifier.
     The falsifier is the load-bearing move. A brief with no falsifier is a recommendation
     wearing a decision's clothes, and the reader can tell.
     Needs: proof-theme.css + proof-blocks.css.  No .fam-* ancestor.  Zero JS.
     ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

<!-- MOVE 1 · THE QUESTION, AND WHAT IS BLOCKED ON IT.
     Frame it as a question with mutually exclusive answers. If you can do two of them, this
     is a plan and not a decision — see the failure branch. -->
<section class="mod open" id="db-question">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">The decision</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">thesis</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#db-question" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="thesis-block">
      <div class="ib-lab">Mutually exclusive &middot; one answer only</div>
      <!-- SLOT · the question. Phrase it so a reader can tell the options apart before
           reading any of them. -->
      <p class="ib-t">Do we fix the mobile layout in <em>CSS</em>, bake a <em>per-screen variant</em>, or run a <em>hybrid</em> that swaps markup only where CSS provably cannot reach?</p>
      <!-- SLOT · what is blocked until this is answered, and by when. A decision with
           nothing blocked on it does not need a brief. -->
      <p class="ib-d">Eight measured layout findings are held pending this call. Three are prose-destroying and cannot ship as they are; the repair for each is a one-line declaration, so <b>the decision is the cost, not the work</b>.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">as-of</b><span class="fv">2026-08-01</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">mobile_PROBE.md R1&ndash;R8</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 2 · ALL OPTIONS, WITH A REAL COST EACH.
     The test for a real cost: could an advocate of that option read it and call it fair?
     A strawman cost is the tell that the decision was already made before the brief. -->
<section class="mod" id="db-options">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">Options</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">table --status</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#db-options" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="tablewrap">
      <table class="data">
        <thead>
          <tr><th>Option</th><th>What it buys</th><th>What it costs</th><th>Status</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <!-- SLOT · one row per option. Every row needs a non-empty cost cell. -->
          <tr>
            <td><span class="cellname">(a) Pure CSS</span></td>
            <td>One artifact. No build step. Reaches pages already published, on their next load.</td>
            <td>Every fix must be expressible as a rule. <b>CSS can wrap, hide, scroll or ellipsise text &mdash; it cannot shorten it</b>, so one measured defect is out of reach.</td>
            <td><span class="pill ok">viable</span></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><span class="cellname">(b) Bake per screen</span></td>
            <td>Arbitrary per-width markup. No specificity arithmetic to lose.</td>
            <td>A build pipeline, N artifacts and the drift between them &mdash; and it was tested: a baked 390&nbsp;px variant authored as <code>grid-template-columns:1fr</code> produced <b>the identical 546&nbsp;px track</b>.</td>
            <td><span class="pill bad">disqualified</span></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td><span class="cellname">(c) Hybrid</span></td>
            <td>Covers the one case CSS provably cannot: a string that is simply too long for the box at any rule.</td>
            <td>A second authoring path, permanently, for a narrow case &mdash; and every future defect will argue for admission to it.</td>
            <td><span class="pill warn">carve-out</span></td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    <div class="callout note">
      <span class="ci" aria-hidden="true">&#9432;</span>
      <div>
        <div class="ctitle">Why (b) is disqualified by measurement, not by taste</div>
        <div class="cbody">The null-transform was run deliberately. <b>The bake buys a build pipeline and delivers the same broken track</b> &mdash; because the failing constraint is intrinsic minimum sizing, which a different markup file inherits unchanged. An option eliminated by a measurement is worth more in a brief than three eliminated by argument.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">options</b><span class="fv">3 &middot; 1 disqualified by test</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">mobile_PROBE.md L21, L29</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 3 · THE HEAD-TO-HEAD, for the two that survived.
     .tradeoff is two columns and no more. If three options survive elimination, cluster
     them: a three-way tradeoff grid stops being readable and starts being a table. -->
<section class="mod" id="db-headtohead">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">(a) against (c)</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">tradeoff</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#db-headtohead" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="tradeoff">
      <!-- SLOT · the case FOR the leaning option. -->
      <div class="tcol pro">
        <div class="th">For (a), everywhere it reaches</div>
        <ul>
          <li>Seven of the eight findings are one-line declarations</li>
          <li>Nothing to build, nothing to keep in sync, nothing to forget to rebuild</li>
          <li>The durable fix is the check, not the rule &mdash; and a check is cheap under (a)</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
      <!-- SLOT · the case AGAINST it, in its own words. Not a softened version. -->
      <div class="tcol con">
        <div class="th">Against (a), honestly</div>
        <ul>
          <li>One finding is a 43&nbsp;px label clipped mid-word to <code>HOW ANSWERS L</code> &mdash; no rule shortens a string</li>
          <li>&ldquo;Expressible as a rule&rdquo; is a constraint that will be re-litigated on every future defect</li>
          <li>Nothing here was verified: every repair is derived from a measured mechanism, none tested</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">mobile_PROBE.md L103&ndash;L109, L155</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 4 · THE LEAN, AND THE FALSIFIER — one block, and they must sit together.
     Splitting them lets a reader take the lean and leave the condition behind, which is
     exactly the failure this recipe exists to prevent. -->
<section class="mod" id="db-lean">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">The call</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">callout</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#db-lean" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="callout insight">
      <span class="ci" aria-hidden="true">&#9670;</span>
      <div>
        <div class="ctitle">Lean</div>
        <!-- SLOT · the lean, with its reason, in one sentence. Name the scope of the carve-out. -->
        <div class="cbody"><b>(a) pure CSS for every layout defect measured, with one narrow (c) carve-out</b> &mdash; scoped to strings that exceed their box at any width, currently exactly one control. The carve-out is written as a named exception rather than a general escape hatch, so admitting a second case is a decision someone has to make out loud.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="callout caution">
      <span class="ci" aria-hidden="true">&#9888;</span>
      <div>
        <div class="ctitle">What would change it</div>
        <!-- SLOT · a concrete, checkable condition. "New information" is not a falsifier.
             If nothing could flip the lean, this is not a decision — see the failure branch. -->
        <div class="cbody">A second defect that needs per-width <i>markup</i> rather than a per-width <i>rule</i>, and whose content is not a too-long string. That would mean the carve-out is not narrow, it is the beginning of (c) &mdash; and (c) should then be adopted deliberately rather than reached by accretion. <b>Recheck at the next full-corpus mobile sweep.</b></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">falsifier</b><span class="fv">stated &middot; checkable &middot; scheduled</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">mobile_PROBE.md L11, L13</span></span>
  </div>
</section>
```

### The Investigation Report
163 lines · 5 blocks · 4 findings · 0 .fam-* deps

```html
<!-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     RECIPE 6 · THE INVESTIGATION REPORT
     the question as asked → the answer, standing alone → ranked findings → what you did
     not look at.
     The last move is the one that makes the first three trustworthy. A report with no named
     blind spot is claiming exhaustiveness, and almost nothing is exhaustive.
     Needs: proof-theme.css + proof-blocks.css.  No .fam-* ancestor.  Zero JS.
     ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

<!-- MOVE 1 · THE QUESTION, VERBATIM, AS IT WAS ACTUALLY ASKED.
     Quoted, not reconstructed. A reconstructed question is always the one you happen to have
     answered, and the reader has no way to notice the substitution. -->
<section class="mod open" id="ir-question">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">The question</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">quote</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#ir-question" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="cite">
      <!-- SLOT · the question, verbatim. If you are paraphrasing, say so here, in this block. -->
      <blockquote>&ldquo;What relation data can we actually get for a ticket, at what call cost &mdash; and does the ticket component need a sibling to show it?&rdquo;</blockquote>
      <div class="src">as posed &middot; read-only probe &middot; <span class="chip up">trusted-upstream</span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">as-of</b><span class="fv">2026-08-01</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">relation-supply-data_PROBE.md</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 2 · THE ANSWER, IN ONE SENTENCE THAT SURVIVES BEING READ ALONE.
     The test: if a reader reads this block and nothing else, are they misled? If yes,
     rewrite it — do not rely on the findings below to rescue it. -->
<section class="mod" id="ir-answer">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">Answer</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">quote --pull</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#ir-answer" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="pull">
      <!-- SLOT · the answer. One sentence. It must stand alone. -->
      <p>Generalise in place, don&rsquo;t build a sibling &mdash; the data is already on the wire, and the shortfall is contract width, not API capability.</p>
      <div class="attr">Answer-first &middot; every response shape below is a real captured call</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">basis</b><span class="fv">4 live reads &middot; 2 query texts read verbatim</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">relation-supply-data_PROBE.md L15, L118</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 3 · FINDINGS, RANKED, EACH WITH ITS GROUND AND ITS CONFIDENCE.
     Rank is a claim: #1 must be above #2 for a reason a reader could dispute. If the findings
     cannot be ranked they are one finding with facets, or a list — use a sequence, not this.
     Confidence is per-finding, never per-report: a report-level confidence word averages away
     exactly the row a reader most needs to discount. -->
<section class="mod" id="ir-findings">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">Findings</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">table --status</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#ir-findings" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="tablewrap">
      <table class="data">
        <thead>
          <tr><th class="num">#</th><th>Finding</th><th>Ground</th><th>Confidence</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <!-- SLOT · one row per finding, most consequential first. Every row needs a ground
               a reader could go and check without you. -->
          <tr>
            <td class="num">1</td>
            <td><span class="cellname">The status and title are already on the wire</span></td>
            <td>The engine&rsquo;s own query returns <code>relatedIssue { identifier title state { name type } }</code> in <b>one call</b>; the MCP path returns <code>{id, title}</code> and nothing else across all 20 entries. Costs <b>zero additional calls</b> &mdash; it is a path switch, not a new capability.</td>
            <td><span class="pill ok">high</span></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td class="num">2</td>
            <td><span class="cellname">Descent is cheap and ascent is not</span></td>
            <td>Ten children returned in one call with <code>hasNextPage: false</code>. A 7-deep ancestor crumb is <b>7 strictly sequential round-trips</b> on MCP &mdash; unparallelisable, because each level&rsquo;s id is the next call&rsquo;s argument.</td>
            <td><span class="pill warn">high&nbsp;/&nbsp;medium</span></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td class="num">3</td>
            <td><span class="cellname">The baked contract is narrower than the API</span></td>
            <td>A live read returns <code>createdBy</code>, <code>projectMilestone</code>, <code>stateHistory[]</code>, <code>attachments[]</code>, <code>documents[]</code>, <code>gitBranchName</code> &mdash; <b>none of which the bake contract has a slot for</b>.</td>
            <td><span class="pill ok">high</span></td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td class="num">4</td>
            <td><span class="cellname">The version constant has already drifted</span></td>
            <td>Code carries <code>PROOF_TICKET_VERSION = 4</code>; the kit reference documents <b>3</b>. A live authoring hazard, found by reading both rather than either.</td>
            <td><span class="pill ok">high</span></td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">confidence</b><span class="fv">per-finding &middot; never averaged</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">relation-supply-data_PROBE.md F1&ndash;F8</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 4 · WHAT WAS NOT LOOKED AT — framed as the questions a sceptical reader will ask.
     Every answer is verdict-led: the first word is the verdict, so the block can be skimmed.
     Naming a blind spot costs one line and buys the rest of the report its credibility. -->
<section class="mod" id="ir-blindspots">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">Blind spots</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">qa</span>
    <span class="mod-aff"><a class="aff mod-perma" href="#ir-blindspots" aria-label="Permalink to this block">&para;</a></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="qa">
      <!-- SLOT · one .qa-row per thing you did NOT do. At least one is mandatory.
           .lead = answered · .lead.warn = partial · .lead.none = not looked at. -->
      <div class="qa-row">
        <div class="qa-q"><span class="mark" aria-hidden="true">Q</span>Did you check the database?</div>
        <div class="qa-a"><span class="lead none">not looked at</span>Out of scope by the directive. Nothing here rests on a database read, and nothing here should be taken as evidence about one.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="qa-row">
        <div class="qa-q"><span class="mark" aria-hidden="true">Q</span>Did you actually run the deep nested query?</div>
        <div class="qa-a"><span class="lead warn">partial</span>The query text was read verbatim; <b>nothing was executed</b>. The single-call cost is reasoned from the absence of <code>first:</code> multipliers, not measured &mdash; which is why finding&nbsp;2 carries a split confidence rather than a high one.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="qa-row">
        <div class="qa-q"><span class="mark" aria-hidden="true">Q</span>What about the activity half of the bake?</div>
        <div class="qa-a"><span class="lead none">not looked at</span>The real baked file carries <code>activity: []</code>, so a populated one could not be measured. Any claim about activity cost is unsupported by this probe.</div>
      </div>
      <div class="qa-row">
        <div class="qa-q"><span class="mark" aria-hidden="true">Q</span>Does anything else depend on the current thin contract?</div>
        <div class="qa-a"><span class="lead warn">unknown</span>Only the producer side was read. If a consumer relies on the contract&rsquo;s narrowness, widening it is a breaking change this report would not have seen.</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-foot">
    <span><b class="fk">prov</b><span class="fv upstream">trusted-upstream</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">named</b><span class="fv">4 blind spots &middot; 2 not looked at &middot; 2 partial</span></span>
    <span><b class="fk">ref</b><span class="fv">relation-supply-data_PROBE.md L22&ndash;L24, L183&ndash;L185</span></span>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- MOVE 5 · THE KEY. -->
<section class="mod flat" id="ir-legend">
  <div class="mod-head">
    <span class="mod-eyebrow">How to read confidence</span>
    <span class="mod-slug">legend</span>
  </div>
  <div class="mod-body">
    <div class="legendbox">
      <div class="row"><span class="mk pill ok">high</span><span class="rowtext"><b>Measured, with the artifact captured.</b> A reader can re-run it from the ground column alone.</span></div>
      <div class="row"><span class="mk pill warn">high / medium</span><span class="rowtext"><b>Split.</b> The existence claim is measured; a second claim inside the same row is reasoned. Splitting the word is the honest form &mdash; one confidence per row averages the two together and hides the weaker half.</span></div>
      <div class="row"><span class="mk"><span class="lead none" style="margin:0">not looked at</span></span><span class="rowtext"><b>A named absence</b>, not a hedge. It says which question this report cannot be cited for.</span></div>
      <div class="row note"><span class="rowtext">Rank is a claim like any other. If you disagree with the order, that is a disputable finding, not a formatting preference.</span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```
